records.statement: Martin-Löf randomness strictly implies computable randomness.
Computable randomness strictly implies Schnorr randomness.
Low for Martin-Löf randomness is equivalent to K-triviality.
Being a base for 1-randomness is equivalent to K-triviality.
Martin-Löf randomness implies constructive dimension 1.
records.caution: No converse is asserted in P1-S001.

records.statement: On an atomless computable probability space, Schnorr randomness is equivalent to T-typicality for every mixing endomorphism, and equivalently for every independent endomorphism, with typicality and effective mixing exactly as in DEF-0056/DEF-0057.
hypotheses: ambient computable probability measure has no atoms
records.caution: The pre-P1-S010 relation was too broad and used the fair-coin DEF-0003 as its source node; the corrected relation is the generalized-space Schnorr notion DEF-0034 and retains atomlessness.

records.statement: In the fair-coin specialization, no-randomness-from-nothing holds for computable randomness but fails for Schnorr randomness for a.e. computable measure-preserving maps; SRC-0015 proves the positive theorem for arbitrary computable Cantor-space source measures and the negative result in Corollary 26.
For fair-coin Cantor space and a.e. computable measure-preserving self-maps, Martin-Löf randoms are the largest subset closed under both randomness conservation and no-randomness-from-nothing.
Martin-Löf randomness strictly implies Kurtz randomness (weak 1-randomness).
records.caution: This is the n=1 instance of the source-stated n-random → weak n-random implication with non-converse.

records.statement: Schnorr randomness strictly implies Kurtz randomness.
Weak 2-randomness strictly implies Martin-Löf randomness.
records.caution: This is the n=1 instance of weak (n+1)-random → n-random, with non-converse explicitly stated in the source.

records.statement: Weak 2-randomness is exactly passing all generalized Martin-Löf tests.
Schnorr randomness is exactly passing all total Solovay tests.
Computable randomness is exactly passing all computably graded tests.
For every n≥1, n-randomness is Martin-Löf randomness relative to ∅^(n−1); this is the jump convention connecting the n-random side of THM-0017 to the oracle-relative framework.
records.caution: This does not identify n-randomness with weak n-randomness DEF-0014.

records.statement: In fair-coin Cantor space, A⊕B is Martin-Löf random exactly when A is Martin-Löf random and B is Martin-Löf random relative to A.
records.caution: A⊕B is even/odd interleaving in SRC-0032; no arbitrary-measure generalization is asserted.

records.statement: For the n=2 instance of DEF-0020, 2-randomness strictly implies Demuth randomness.
records.caution: This relation is only the n=2 instance of DEF-0020; it is not a claim that arbitrary n-randomness has been compared separately with Demuth randomness.

records.statement: Demuth randomness strictly implies difference randomness.
Weak 2-randomness strictly implies difference randomness.
Difference randomness strictly implies Martin-Löf randomness.
Demuth randomness and weak 2-randomness are incomparable.
records.caution: SRC-0035 supplies separation properties in both directions; this is not inferred from the definitions.

records.statement: Balanced randomness strictly implies Oberwolfach randomness.
Oberwolfach randomness strictly implies difference randomness.
Balanced randomness strictly implies difference randomness.
records.caution: Recorded because SRC-0036 explicitly supplies it; not merely inferred by transitivity.

records.statement: For the n=2 instance of DEF-0020, 2-randomness strictly implies weak 2-randomness.
records.caution: Specifically 2-randomness → weak 2-randomness; DEF-0020 remains the general jump-indexed family.

records.statement: Martin-Löf randomness on computable probability spaces is conserved by morphisms; isomorphisms restrict to inverse computable bijections on the random-point sets.
Schnorr randomness on computable probability spaces is conserved by morphisms.
Computable randomness with respect to computable Cantor-space measures satisfies no-randomness-from-nothing for μ-a.e. computable maps to their pushforward measures.
Computable randomness is invariant under a.e.-computable measure-preserving isomorphisms between computable probability measures on Cantor space, with inverse identities holding on random points.
Schnorr randomness fails no-randomness-from-nothing for the a.e.-computable measure-preserving Cantor-space map class of SRC-0015.

Across all computable probability measures on Cantor space, the point/measure pairs that are Martin-Löf random form the largest class closed under both randomness conservation and no-randomness-from-nothing.
Every computable probability space admits a binary representation/isomorphism-on-full-measure-domain by Cantor space with an appropriate computable probability measure.
If the computable probability measure is atomless, the computable probability space is a computable Lebesgue space in the sense of SRC-0012.
Every 1-generic real is weakly 1-generic.

support.pointer: genericity discussion/Property 1.2; weak 1-genericity is presented as a generalization of 1-genericity
meet-or-avoid versus dense-meeting definitions in the introduction

records.caution: P1-S006 records only implication here; no same-level strictness claim is promoted without a separately inspected source statement.

records.statement: For n≥1, (n+1)-genericity strictly implies weak (n+1)-genericity.
records.caution: This relation is parameter-shifted exactly as stated; it does not collapse the two genericity hierarchies.

records.statement: For n≥1, weak (n+1)-genericity strictly implies n-genericity.
records.caution: The target index is n while the source index is n+1.

records.statement: Weak 1-genericity strictly implies Kurtz randomness (weak 1-randomness).
records.caution: This is a source-stated category-to-measure comparison. It does not identify the smallness frameworks or justify analogous implications at other levels.

records.statement: For reals α∈(0,1], α is left-c.e. iff α is the halting probability of some prefix-free/self-delimiting partial computable machine.
records.caution: The witnessing machine need not be universal, so this equivalence carries no randomness conclusion.

records.statement: Chaitin Ω-numbers are exactly the Martin-Löf-random left-c.e. reals in the unit interval.
records.caution: The characterization requires both left-c.e. approximation and Martin-Löf randomness and requires the witnessing machine to be universal.

records.statement: Every Chaitin Ω-number is left-c.e.
records.caution: The converse fails without the additional Martin-Löf-randomness hypothesis; see REL-0039.

records.statement: The binary expansion of every Chaitin Ω-number is Martin-Löf random.
records.caution: The conclusion is about the infinite binary expansion of Ω_U, not the finite program strings in dom(U); the expansion convention is DEF-0045.

records.statement: A P-time stretching function ensemble is a pseudorandom generator in SRC-0049 exactly when its output distribution on a uniform seed and the uniform distribution of the same output length satisfy the source's computational-indistinguishability requirement.
records.caution: This relation is between finite-string distribution ensembles; it is not an implication to or from any individual-sequence algorithmic-randomness definition.

records.statement: An infinite sequence is Δ-random exactly when every Δ-computable martingale fails to succeed on it.
records.caution: The resource parameter Δ, including the polynomial-time specialization p=p1, is essential. No unbounded-randomness hierarchy edge is inferred.

records.statement: Δ1^1-randomness is equivalent to Δ1^1-Martin-Löf randomness.
records.caution: This equivalence is specific to the inspected Δ1^1 setting and does not collapse the Π1^1 notions.

records.statement: Π1^1-randomness strictly implies Π1^1-Martin-Löf randomness.
records.caution: The two Π1^1 labels are not synonyms.

records.statement: Π1^1-Martin-Löf randomness strictly implies Δ1^1-randomness.
records.caution: DEF-0050 is also equivalent to Δ1^1-Martin-Löf randomness DEF-0051, but not to Π1^1-Martin-Löf randomness.

records.statement: Π1^1-randomness strictly implies higher weak 2-randomness.
records.caution: Higher weak 2-randomness is the higher Π^ck_2 level, not ordinary weak 2-randomness DEF-0015.

records.statement: Higher weak 2-randomness strictly implies Δ1^1-randomness.
records.caution: This is a source-stated higher-hierarchy edge, not an extrapolation from finite weak-n randomness.

records.statement: Higher weak 2-randomness strictly implies higher difference randomness.
records.caution: The source factors the implication through higher Oberwolfach randomness and supplies a separation; no lower stronger-test edge is imported.

records.statement: Martin-Löf randomness with respect to a computable Cantor-space measure yields Birkhoff convergence for computable measure-preserving transformations and computable observables; under ergodicity the limit is the expectation, with stronger ergodic effective-set/lower-semicomputable-observable forms in SRC-0057.
records.caution: Keep the nonergodic convergence conclusion separate from the ergodic equality-to-expectation conclusion.

records.statement: Martin-Löf random points in a computable probability space satisfy the source-stated effective Birkhoff conclusions for μ-layerwise computable, measure-preserving, ergodic transformations and the corresponding effective/layerwise-effective observables.
hypotheses: T is μ-layerwise computable, measure-preserving and ergodic

records.statement: In fair-coin Cantor space, Martin-Löf randomness is exactly the property of having convergent Birkhoff averages for every computable measure-preserving transformation and every computable observable in the Franklin-Towsner setting.
records.caution: This characterization is fair-coin Cantor-space and nonergodic; it is not generalized to arbitrary computable probability spaces in P1-S010.

records.statement: Weak 2-randomness in fair-coin Cantor space implies convergence of Birkhoff averages for every computable measure-preserving transformation and every lower semicomputable observable in SRC-0058's setting.
records.caution: No equality-to-expectation is asserted without ergodicity, and no generalized-measure version is inferred.

records.statement: A Martin-Löf random point in a computable probability space cannot remain forever inside an effectively open set of measure less than one under a μ-layerwise computable, measure-preserving, ergodic transformation.
records.caution: Recorded as the recurrence interface used by the principal effective-ergodic theorem, not as a converse characterization.
